title: Universal Controller Update
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.0 is the first major architecture expansion of the project, generalizing the physical-input layer from a T.Flight-oriented workflow into persistent universal DirectInput controller management. It adds a durable multi-device registry, automatic low-frequency controller discovery, explicit controller selection and verification, per-device calibration and vJoy requirement memory, ambiguity-safe reconnect and switching behavior, a new Overview dashboard, stronger HidHide self-access handling, system-tray operation, controller-specific troubleshooting/reset tools, in-app uninstall access, and a more unified Settings/controller-management experience while keeping discovery, persistence, UI, setup, repair, and tray work outside the low-latency DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: DEPRECATED: v2.0.0 contains a launch-blocking startup defect in the new system-tray integration. The tray menu can initialize under QGuiApplication even though the Qt Widgets tray path requires QApplication, causing the mapper to exit during startup instead of opening and running normally. Do not install or use v2.0.0. Upgrade to v2.0.1 or newer, which corrects the startup object and strengthens packaged Qt Widgets and upgrade-path validation.
highlights: Generalizes the mapper from a primarily T.Flight-oriented physical-input workflow into a persistent universal DirectInput controller platform without moving controller-management work into the report-processing hot path.

Adds a persistent verified-controller registry with layered HID, DirectInput, product, vendor/product, and capability identity matching so known hardware can be recognized across reconnects and restarts.

Stores controller-specific calibration, remembered vJoy capability requirements, verification state, and offline device memory per physical device instead of allowing setup data to leak between unrelated controllers.
Adds low-frequency DirectInput inventory and arrival/removal discovery that tracks attached physical controllers while explicitly excluding vJoy from physical input selection.

Adds an Input Controllers / Controller Manager experience that shows connected, verified, new, active, and remembered-offline devices together and supports refresh, setup/verification, active-device selection, and forgetting remembered hardware.
Uses ambiguity-safe controller matching: identical or insufficiently distinguishable devices are not silently selected, preventing automatic binding to the wrong physical controller.

Known healthy controllers can reconnect quietly, while newly discovered controllers enter the themed Verify Setup flow only when selection, calibration, readiness, or verification actually requires user attention.

Adds optional intelligent controller switching that only auto-selects when exactly one eligible verified device is unambiguous, preserving explicit user selection when multiple plausible devices exist.

Adds a new Overview landing page summarizing the active physical controller, vJoy output, setup/readiness health, current configuration, mapping state, and presentation-smoothed performance metrics while Diagnostics remains the raw engineering view.
Improves HidHide handling with explicit detection of mapper self-access blocking, including cases where HidHide can prevent the physical controller from appearing to the app at all.

Adds a narrow HidHide allowlist-only repair path and installer-time registration of the installed mapper executable where permitted, while preserving unrelated HidHide application and hidden-device entries.
Adds native system-tray operation with controlled close-to-tray behavior and a concise tray menu so the mapper can remain available without occupying the main window.

Adds controller-only troubleshooting/reset tools so broken controller setup state can be cleared without indiscriminately deleting profiles, mappings, curves, Automation, or unrelated application configuration.
Adds an in-app uninstaller entry and safer uninstall defaults that retain shared dependencies and user data unless the user deliberately chooses otherwise.

Standardizes controller/setup controls inside Settings so controller selection, readiness, verification, troubleshooting, HidHide/vJoy status, and related maintenance actions are presented as one coherent workflow.

Keeps controller discovery, registry persistence, setup/readiness inspection, HidHide work, tray behavior, Overview smoothing, and uninstall/reset operations outside the DirectInput-to-vJoy report loop so the existing low-latency mapper architecture remains isolated.

title: Startup & Upgrade Hotfix
summary: Fixes a launch-blocking issue introduced in v2.0.0 where the system-tray menu could initialize under QGuiApplication instead of the required QApplication. v2.0.1 also strengthens packaged Qt Widgets validation and the v1.9.3 to v2 upgrade acceptance path while preserving existing configuration and mapper performance.
statusNote: Startup and upgrade hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.2 for dashboard, settings, tray, and controller-switching polish.
highlights: Replaces the mapper's QGuiApplication startup object with QApplication for the existing Qt Widgets tray menu.
Fails packaging when Qt6Widgets.dll is absent and adds deterministic Widgets/tray-menu startup coverage.
Validates clean install, v1.9.3 schema-14 upgrade, already-migrated schema-15 recovery, and the published built-in updater chain.
Logs an immediate mapper startup exit as a failed launch handoff rather than treating installer success as complete update success.
Preserves Universal Controller Update behavior, user profiles, curves, mappings, buttons, POVs, Automation, preferences, and the mapper hot path.

title: Dashboard & UX Polish
summary: v2.0.2 gives the Universal Controller Update the interface it deserves, with a redesigned Overview dashboard, standardized Settings experience, polished theme-aware tray controls, and a permanent global mapping control. It also completes per-controller vJoy requirement enforcement during device switching and hardens new-device verification when multiple controllers are connected.
statusNote: Dashboard and UX polish release; upgrade to v2.0.3 for multi-controller setup and vJoy reliability fixes.
highlights: Replaces the card-stack Overview with a signal-flow dashboard for physical input, HOTAS BF6 processing, vJoy output, health, capability, and smoothed performance state.
Places the theme-aware mapping state and Start or Stop action permanently in the main header and removes the Axis-page duplicate.
Reorganizes Settings into aligned responsive sections and separates maintenance from the confirmation-protected uninstaller.
Applies Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun visual tokens to the existing reliable Qt tray menu.
Validates saved target vJoy requirements during controller switching, preserves adequate existing output supersets, and blocks mapping restoration until valid output is available.
Explicitly acquires and verifies a selected new controller regardless of another controller's connection state.

title: Multi-Controller Setup & vJoy Reliability Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.3 hardens the Universal Controller workflow using real multi-controller hardware testing. It fixes incorrect setup targeting when a new controller is connected, completes NEW-to-VERIFIED persistence after automatic repair, ensures vJoy capacity is actually sufficient for each verified controller, makes disconnected devices visually unmistakable, cleans generic controller terminology, and fixes remaining Settings layout and styling regressions.
statusNote: Multi-controller reliability hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.4 for the UI responsiveness fix.
highlights: Removes the mapper-ownership shortcut that treated a BUSY vJoy device with successful reports as sufficient without validating axes, buttons, and POV capacity.
Configures and reinspects the actual selected vJoy device before setup can become Ready, including the safe first-time physical button-capacity floor and saved controller-specific requirements.
Carries explicit DirectInput controller identity from new-device discovery into a themed setup selector, so a newly connected controller never opens verification for an already active controller.
Completes post-repair validation by immediately saving or updating the selected controller, clearing NEW and preserving VERIFIED after the setup popup closes.
Distinguishes active connected, selected offline, verified, new, and offline saved controllers; adds an intentional zero-connected state and clear automatic-switch feedback.
Repairs compact Settings-row text layout, fully themes the vJoy +/- selector and theme menu controls, and uses Controller or Device terminology for generic physical inputs.

Keeps Universal Controller discovery, registry persistence, readiness inspection, verification, driver transactions, UI rendering, and all new state handling outside the DirectInput-to-vJoy report loop.

title: UI Responsiveness Hotfix
summary: Fixes a severe UI responsiveness regression where broad high-frequency state notifications caused expensive controller and device presentation work to be repeatedly reevaluated. v2.0.4 separates telemetry from controller and configuration state, caches controller presentation data, and restores smooth responsiveness without changing the mapper hot path.
statusNote: UI responsiveness hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.5 for published updater acceptance reliability.
highlights: Replaces the 16 ms broad state notification with dedicated input and telemetry notifications, so slow Settings and controller bindings stay idle while live metrics remain responsive.
Caches the controller presentation model behind a dedicated controllersChanged notification and only publishes a replacement after a material change.
Compares low-frequency DirectInput inventory snapshots before matching or rebuilding the controller model, leaving unchanged discovery ticks quiet.
Uses one Settings-page controller-model reference and a cached connected-controller count rather than repeatedly calling the C++ controller property in QML loops.
Adds focused notification/cache contract coverage and a ten-second steady-state controller-model validation while preserving DirectInput discovery cadence and mapper behavior.

title: Published Updater Acceptance Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.5 fixes the headless GitHub Actions environment used to validate the public v1.9.3 built-in updater path. It preserves v2.0.4 UI responsiveness behavior and all shipped mapper code while making the isolated acceptance launch the updated Qt application with the same offscreen platform used by existing installer smoke tests.
statusNote: Published updater acceptance hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.6 for public latest-manifest readiness validation.
highlights: Sets the Qt offscreen platform only inside the isolated published-updater acceptance so the v1.9.3 launcher, helper, installer, updated launcher, and updated mapper can be exercised on a non-interactive GitHub-hosted Windows runner.
Leaves user installs, normal desktop mapper startup, controller input, vJoy output, and the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path unchanged.
Emits the updater log on an acceptance startup failure, making a future public-update handoff failure diagnosable from its CI receipt.

title: Published Manifest Readiness Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.6 fixes a release-acceptance race in which GitHub could publish a release before its public latest-manifest alias advanced. The v1.9.3 updater acceptance now waits for the exact latest endpoint that the shipped launcher consumes to identify the expected release before exercising the unchanged full update path.
statusNote: Published manifest readiness hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.7 for correct hosted-runner manifest decoding.
highlights: Waits for the public latest update manifest to report the candidate version and tag before launching the unchanged v1.9.3 updater.
Bounds that wait to five minutes and records the last observed public manifest state if GitHub release metadata does not become ready.
Preserves all packaged mapper, controller, vJoy, DirectInput-to-vJoy report-path, installer, helper, and configuration-migration behavior from v2.0.5.

title: Published Manifest Transport Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.7 corrects a GitHub Actions-only manifest-decoding flaw exposed by the v2.0.6 readiness gate. The acceptance now obtains the JSON manifest through PowerShell's REST client, which decodes GitHub release assets correctly on hosted Windows while still querying the exact latest URL consumed by the shipped v1.9.3 launcher.
statusNote: Published manifest transport hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.8 for corrected One-Sided transfer semantics and workflow reliability fixes.
highlights: Uses Invoke-RestMethod to decode the public latest update-manifest JSON correctly on the GitHub-hosted Windows runner.
Retains v2.0.6's bounded exact-version and exact-tag readiness guard before launching the unchanged v1.9.3 updater.
Preserves all mapper, controller, vJoy, DirectInput-to-vJoy report-path, installer, helper, startup, and configuration-migration behavior from v2.0.6.

title: Runtime and Workflow Reliability Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.8 corrects the real runtime semantics of One-Sided axes and restores reliable selected-axis Curve Editor telemetry while applying narrow Profiles, calibration, vJoy-capacity, and Automation workflow fixes. The DirectInput-to-vJoy report path remains compiled and allocation-free.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.0.9 Final v2 Reliability Cleanup.
highlights: One-Sided axes now run from the former bipolar midpoint at 0% to the positive endpoint at 100%, with below-origin clamping, a low-end deadzone, and unipolar inversion.
Axes and Curve Editor share the same one-sided domain for curves, custom points, effective traces, labels, and live telemetry without recompiling curves on movement.
Profiles use a fully themed overflow menu and themed rename/delete controls in Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun; legacy direct controls migrate to visible Automation rules.
Calibration records bounded durable success history, and vJoy readiness uses complete profile and Automation requirements.

title: Final v2 Reliability Cleanup
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.9 closes four remaining issues found during real v2.0.8 hardware validation: automatic vJoy repair now completes verification in one pass and reports exact required capacity correctly, physical calibration ignores phantom axes and distinguishes centered from non-centering controls, Automation parameter editors reliably mutate and display the correct action row, and Centered/One-Sided output limits retain independent values across range changes.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.0.10 Virtual Output Layouts & Phantom-Axis Safety.
highlights: Automatic repair polls the actual vJoy capability at a bounded control-plane cadence before the same transaction continues to verification and worker reacquisition.
Exact required vJoy capacity is Ready across header, Overview, Settings, Diagnostics, and Verify Setup; 32 buttons remains optional informational headroom.
Two-stage calibration excludes unobserved slots, stores stable interior rests as centered, and accepts stable endpoint controls as range-only without profile-range assumptions.
Automation condition and action delegates use explicit row indexes so every selector and editor updates the intended draft record.
Configuration schema 17 persists separate Centered and One-Sided output-limit ranges and migrates schema-16 active limits safely.

title: Virtual Output Layouts & Phantom-Axis Safety
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.10 introduces reusable per-profile virtual-output layouts so Battlefield 6 sees one deliberate vJoy descriptor at a time. It adds exact-axis descriptor verification, profile-owned layout selection, safe neutral/release/reacquire transitions, calibration-backed physical-axis activity classification, and truthful NOT ROUTED telemetry without adding allocation, UI, driver, or HidHide work to the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.0.11 Virtual Output Visibility Completion.
highlights: Profiles persist a selected reusable virtual-output layout; the built-in BF6 Output layout exposes exactly X, Y, Z, and Rz with 32-button capacity, while an explicit 5-axis layout can be prepared on a separate vJoy device.
Readiness now treats virtual-axis descriptors as exact: additional or missing axes require an explicit setup correction, while button and native-POV capacity remain minimum-capacity checks.

An active layout change neutralizes the prior virtual device, releases it, applies only pre-authorized HidHide visibility changes for exact stored virtual-device identities, then acquires and establishes a neutral baseline on the selected output.

Completed calibration classifies advertised physical axes as Active or Fixed from observed travel. Fixed slots are never routed or offered as Automation input, while the UI continues to report the full DirectInput descriptor honestly.

Schema 18 migrates existing configurations data-only into a preserved layout derived from their existing routes, buttons, and POVs; migration does not rewrite vJoy configuration or discard saved calibration, profiles, controller memory, or Automation.

title: Virtual Output Visibility Completion
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.11 completes the safe practical HidHide isolation path for reusable virtual-output layouts. It adds an explicit exact-vJoy HID adoption step, preserves v2.0.10's neutral/release/acquire transition, and reports physical/output capability state concisely without adding work to the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.0.12 Automation Editor Interaction Qualification. Prepare an exact vJoy identity in Settings before relying on automatic inactive-output visibility, and restart a game that was already running when its controller handle was opened.
highlights: A layout can be marked visibility-managed only after HidHide confirms the exact user-selected HID\VID_1234&PID_BEAD vJoy instance is currently enumerated; display names, inferred ownership, and unrelated devices are never accepted.

Normal cross-layout switching stays non-elevated: it neutralizes and releases the old output, hides only adopted inactive layouts, exposes the selected adopted layout, acquires it, and publishes a neutral baseline before mapping resumes. A failed visibility command rolls back completed visibility changes.

Settings exposes one compact preparation action for the selected layout, and Controller Diagnostics now reports advertised/active/fixed physical axes, active profile/output descriptor, and managed output visibility without exposing arbitrary device inventories.
HidHide changes game-device enumeration, not already-open game handles. Switch layouts before launching a game, or restart a game that retains an older controller handle after the switch.
Configuration schema 18 remains compatible: existing layouts stay untouched and un-managed until their exact virtual HID identities are explicitly adopted.

title: Automation Editor Interaction Qualification
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.12 locks down the final v2 Automation-editor reliability path with an offscreen QML interaction qualification. It preserves v2.0.11 virtual-output visibility behavior, the v2.0.9 stable-index editor correction, and the allocation-free DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.1.0 Profile Library & Portable Configuration. v2.0.12 adds automated interaction coverage for the Automation editor; physical controller, installer, and game acceptance remain machine-specific checks.
highlights: Executes the real AutomationPage QML draft logic for each of the fourteen available action types and verifies the resulting action draft type.
Exercises independent edits across multiple action and condition rows, preserving the explicit stable-delegate-index contract that prevents nested signal-index collisions.
Retains the parameter-editor contract for virtual buttons, profiles, sensitivity, output adjustments, limits, forced values, mixes, follows, taps, and mapping controls.
Does not change MappingWorker, DirectInput polling, vJoy writes, driver configuration, persistence, or the v2.0.11 exact-HID virtual-output visibility implementation.

title: Profile Library & Portable Configuration
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.1.0 adds a game-aware Profile Library and validated portable Profile/Pack configuration exchange without changing the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.1.1 Profile Library Completion & Portable Pack Safety. v2.1.0 established the profile-category and portable configuration foundation; v2.1.1 completes selective export, compatibility preview, explicit conflicts, and opt-in calibration handling.
highlights: Introduces category-aware profiles with scoped names, defaults, restore-last behavior, safe moves/duplicates/deletes, optional enable state, and stable references for mapping controls and Automation.
Adds a shared Profile Library across Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun for cards, category behavior, profile detail, curve/Automation/output context, and direct navigation to existing editors.
Offers optional foreground executable category selection at a low control-plane cadence; it is disabled/enabled in Settings and does not alter DirectInput polling or report processing.

Exports and imports versioned .hbf6profile and .hbf6pack files with strict bounds, preview-before-apply, atomic validation, collision-safe ID remapping, and conservative local-data preservation. Device descriptors and calibration are off by default, and imported calibration is retained only for review.

Schema 19 migrates existing user profiles into General without guessing game names or changing mappings, curves, buttons, POVs, Automation, output layouts, controller memory, vJoy configuration, or hardware drivers.
No mapper report-loop work was added: profile category management, portability, UI details, detection, persistence, and device/calibration handling remain on control/configuration paths.

title: Profile Library Completion & Portable Pack Safety
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.1.1 completes the Profile Library portability workflow with selective pack export, independent strict Profile/Pack schemas, detailed pre-apply preview, explicit category/profile conflict decisions, compatible controller matching, and opt-in calibration application without changing the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.1.2 Deep Tray & Runtime Efficiency. v2.1.1 remains the completed Profile Library portability baseline; v2.1.2 preserves it while reducing unnecessary minimized and tray-hidden presentation work.
highlights: Pack export selects whole categories or individual profiles and carries only the requested related configuration; required custom curves and vJoy contracts remain closed over so a selected profile cannot be exported with broken dependencies.

The transfer center previews category rules, profile mapping/POV/Automation counts, profile-control relationships, curves, vJoy requirements, source/current controller compatibility, conflicts, and warnings before import can mutate saved configuration.

Profile and Pack schemas are independently versioned and reject unsupported future formats, dangling relationship references, invalid vJoy layouts, duplicate dependencies, and unsafe device descriptors before the atomic candidate is committed.

Existing categories use explicit Merge, Import as New, or protected Replace behavior. Profile collisions use renamed copies by default; destructive category/profile replacement requires a separate confirmation.

Devices and calibration are opt-in on export. Calibration remains local by default and can apply only to an explicitly selected compatible saved controller; ambiguous matches never select by controller name.
No work was added to mapper report processing. The synthetic report benchmark covers all built-in curve families plus profile controls and Automation with zero hot-path allocations.

title: Deep Tray & Runtime Efficiency
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.1.2 makes minimized and tray-hidden presentation work sleep aggressively while preserving the fully awake, allocation-free DirectInput-to-vJoy mapper.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.1.3 Profiles, Categories & Game Detection UX. v2.1.2 remains the Deep Tray and runtime-efficiency baseline; upgrade for the clearer Profile/Category workflow and smarter game detection.
highlights: Introduces explicit Visible, Minimized, and Tray Hidden presentation lifecycle states outside the mapper. Snapshot projection remains responsive while visible, reduces to 200 ms while minimized, and stops in Deep Tray Sleep.

Restoring from the tray immediately projects current runtime state and resumes visible presentation cadence without restarting MappingWorker, changing Mapping On/Off intent, releasing vJoy, or mutating profiles and configuration.

Uses safe Qt Quick nonpersistent scene-graph and graphics-resource controls plus releaseResources() on tray entry, so the GUI can recreate resources on restore without destroying the backend or real-time worker.
Defers Overview, Settings, Profile Library, Curve Editor, and Automation QML-tree creation until first use while retaining a loaded page to protect unsaved editor/import drafts from navigation loss.
Adapts presentation controller discovery to visible, minimized, and tray-hidden cadence while leaving worker-owned physical reconnect correctness independent of the UI timer.
Stops the optional foreground game-category detection timer when the feature is disabled; enabled detection remains a separate one-second control-plane sample.
Does not alter DirectInput polling, transforms, Automation runtime evaluation, vJoy report scheduling, output-layout behavior, HidHide configuration, persistence, or the synthetic report path.

title: Profiles, Categories & Game Detection UX
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.1.3 makes game-aware configuration clear and direct: categories show their activation behavior, game rules are managed in place, and profile detail becomes a compact configuration dashboard without changing the real-time DirectInput-to-vJoy mapper.
statusNote: Superseded by v2.1.4 Runtime Responsiveness & GUI Efficiency. v2.1.3 retains the Profile/Category workflow while v2.1.4 moves discovery off the GUI event loop and reduces presentation churn. Physical controller, game, installer, signing, public updater, and measured resource acceptance remain machine- or release-specific checks.
highlights: Profile Library cards now explain Game Detection to Category to Profile to Virtual Output, summarizing linked games, activation behavior, profile counts, and the active context without exposing implementation detail.
Category pages separate Automatic Activation from the explicit Restore Last-used Profile or Always Use a Specific Profile choice. The default selector appears only for the fixed-profile behavior.

Add Game is a themed workflow for currently running applications, an EXE browser, or an advanced manual executable. Existing executable rules remain compatible and are normalized to Windows case-insensitive basenames.

The detector takes a bounded one-second process snapshot outside MappingWorker. An active matching category wins; otherwise persisted category order is the deterministic tie-breaker, and unchanged snapshots do not reapply a profile.

Themed Profile, Category, and Pack import/export choices preserve existing strict preview-before-apply validation and safe conflict decisions. Profile detail summarizes mappings, curves, Automation, output readiness, and game/category relationships instead of reproducing the editor.

Settings, Automation, Profiles, and Overview share the exact established Legacy card surface used by Axes, Buttons, Curve Editor, Calibration, and Diagnostics. Standard and Top Gun retain their existing theme treatments.
No DirectInput polling, vJoy report scheduling, configuration serialization migration, allocation, locking, file work, process enumeration, UI work, or logging was added to the mapper report loop.

title: Runtime Responsiveness & GUI Efficiency
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.1.4 removes unnecessary GUI-thread work and high-frequency presentation churn, then unloads inactive QML page trees, so the mapper remains responsive while games, browsers, launchers, Discord, and other desktop applications are running.
statusNote: Historical stable release. v2.1.4 established the responsive control-plane and unloadable page lifecycle baseline; v2.2.0 is the current recommended release. Physical controller, game, installer, signing, public updater, and live packaged-resource acceptance remain machine- or release-specific checks.
highlights: Windows process enumeration and DirectInput controller inventory discovery run on low-priority control-plane threads. The Qt/UI thread receives completed snapshots only, while MappingWorker remains independent.

Automatic game detection keeps case-insensitive basename matching, active-category preference, deterministic category tie-breaking, unchanged-set suppression, and slower visible/minimized/tray-hidden cadence. The explicit Add Game list also receives asynchronous cached snapshots.

Visible analog and POV presentation runs at approximately 30 Hz, numeric telemetry at 10 Hz, and percentile sampling at four Hz. Minimized and tray-hidden control-plane work remains reduced or asleep.
The 128-button presentation model is cached and changes only for configuration, topology, or an actual button/runtime state transition; broad axis telemetry cannot rebuild it.

Leaving any main page unloads its QML tree, including diagnostics, Canvas-backed curve editing, and button-card delegates. Unsaved Automation editing and Profile Library import choices are retained only as compact shell-owned state and restore when their page is reopened.

Focused test instrumentation records UI notification rates, discovery background completions, structural rebuild counts, and Qt event-loop delays above 16, 50, 100, and 250 milliseconds only when enabled for tests.

The offscreen page-lifecycle qualification cycles all nine pages 20 times across Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun; it requires one live page and no retained QML objects after a completed cycle, checks draft/import preservation, and records Windows working-set and private-byte samples.
No DirectInput report-loop, transform, Automation, vJoy scheduling, allocation, mutex, storage, process-inspection, or UI-control change was made to MappingWorker.

title: Input Learning, Quick Assign & vJoy Capacity Correction
summary: Makes the existing mapping model substantially easier to operate with control-plane input learning, guided axis assignment, clearer control naming, and a corrected minimum vJoy button-capacity calculation while preserving the allocation-free DirectInput-to-vJoy mapper.
statusNote: Historical stable release. v2.1.5 remains a valid record of the input-learning and vJoy-capacity correction baseline; v2.2.0 is the current recommended release.
highlights: Learn Input observes the existing UI/control-plane physical snapshot and guided Axis Quick Assign uses configured game-output aliases without adding report-loop work.
Button custom names gained stable inline editing, while Axis Name and Game Output Name retain dedicated editing drafts protected from live telemetry refresh.
vJoy readiness calculates button requirements from actual mapped button/POV routes and enabled Automation actions instead of treating provisioned layout capacity as required.
No DirectInput polling, mapping evaluation, vJoy write, allocation, lock, string, UI, or learning-state branch was added to MappingWorker's report path.

title: Input Learning & Quick Map Correction
summary: Corrects physical-versus-virtual button identity, makes route conflicts explicit and safe, adds guided Button Quick Map, and polishes themed learning controls while preserving the allocation-free DirectInput-to-vJoy mapper.
statusNote: Historical stable release. v2.1.6 remains the completed input-learning and Quick Map correction baseline; v2.2.0 is the current recommended release.
highlights: Learn Input freezes its intended virtual button before physical detection and uses the same explicit Replace, Ignore, and Cancel route-conflict choices as manual assignment and Quick Map.
Axis Quick Map re-arms after a bounded stability window, Button Quick Map waits for held buttons to release, and both keep completed assignments if the workflow exits early.
Themed learning controls keep physical and virtual button identity explicit while shared-output fan-in remains a logical OR in the compiled mapping table.
Learning, conflict decisions, naming, dialogs, and Quick Map state remain on the UI/control plane; MappingWorker receives no new learning-state checks, strings, locks, allocations, or conflict work.

title: Bumpless Curve / Mapping Transition Smoothing
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.2.0 prevents mapper-created virtual-axis jumps during curve and mapping changes while retaining immediate physical-input response and the allocation-free DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: Current recommended release for compatible DirectInput controllers. v2.2.0 has focused local core, migration, QML-startup, UI-contract, automation, and synthetic hot-path evidence. Physical controller, game, installer, signing, published updater, and live packaged-resource acceptance remain release- and machine-specific checks.
highlights: Each material compiled-mapping transition anchors to the actual virtual output, evaluates the new mapping immediately, and decays only the correction offset over an optional 0–1000 ms duration (100 ms default).

The correction cancels when the player moves the physical control aggressively, and rapid toggles use the current actual output as the next anchor so transitions remain continuous without input filtering.
Global Settings and Profile Library expose themed enablement, duration, and explicit profile inherit/override controls across Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun.
Schema 20 persists global and per-profile settings with deterministic enabled/100 ms defaults for legacy configuration and no rewrite of existing mappings, curves, Automation, or output layouts.

Focused tests prove both transition directions, direct new-mapping response, rapid toggles, tiny-change suppression, opposite-output reversal, zero/disabled behavior, user-intent cancellation, independent axes, and migration persistence.

The synthetic report benchmark reports zero hot-path allocations in the normal steady state. No per-report heap allocation, lock, logging, persistence, process discovery, or UI work was added to MappingWorker.
